item.title: How AI Changes the Way Teams Work. Not Just How Fast They Work
item.description: New research reveals the real job AI does in teams: it eliminates social coordination overhead, letting humans focus on strategic work. Instead of managing personalities and reading emotional cues, workers give instructions and review outputs while AI handles execution.

item.title: Nature Study: AI Boosts Performance but Hurts Motivation and Autonomy
item.description: AI solves the "produce better content" job but fails the "develop capable, engaged workers" job. New research shows that while AI collaboration improves immediate output quality, it doesn't build human skills and leaves people less motivated for independent work.

item.title: Why 75% of AI Investments Fail and How Purpose-Driven Strategy Delivers Results
item.description: IBM's study reveals only 25% of AI initiatives deliver expected ROI. The problem? Companies start with technology and hope it finds purpose. Successful organizations flip this approach, they begin with clear business outcomes, then determine if AI can help.

item.title: Top 8 Books to Build Human-Centered AI Systems That Actually Work
item.description: AI will transform your organisation, but will that transformation serve people or replace them? These eight books provide the roadmap for human-centred AI: aligning technology with human purpose, designing collaboration, and creating systems that elevate rather than displace human work.

item.title: Why Treating AI as a Teammate Will Define the Next Decade of Work
item.description: The productivity gains from AI are real: 14% faster problem-solving, 50% faster coding. But treating AI as just another tool fails. Organizations succeeding treat it as a teammate with defined roles, transparent reasoning, and human oversight matched to risk. New rules for a new team.

item.title: Mapping Tasks to AI Control Modes: A Practical Framework for Safe, Scalable Adoption
item.description: Minutes saved don’t equal business value. This article shows how to assign AI tasks to the right control mode—Tool, Co-Pilot, Partner, or Supervised Autonomy—based on ambiguity and consequence. Build scalable governance that turns AI adoption into measurable performance gains.

item.title: New Research Shows AI Coding Tools Make Developers 19% Slower on Real Projects
item.description: A METR study found that AI coding tools like Cursor Pro and Claude slowed experienced developers by 19%, even though they felt 24% faster—revealing a major gap between perceived and actual productivity.

item.title: AI Collaboration and Human Judgment: The Real Driver of Organisational Impact
item.description: AI delivers measurable gains in quality and speed, yet organisational impact varies widely. The determining factor is not technical literacy but human judgment. How professionals decide when to rely, verify or question AI shapes outcomes, responsibility and long-term transformation.
